newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat in mostly good to excellent condition.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat in mostly good to excellent condition.

text.p: The Kansas winter wheat crop remained in mostly good to excellent condition during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop weather report.
Wheat condition was rated 19 percent excellent, 68 good, 11 fair and two poor. That compared to last week's rating of 20 percent excellent, 64 good, 13 fair and three poor.

Wind damage to the crop was reported to be two percent moderate, 13 percent light and 85 percent undamaged. Wheat freeze damage remained steady at one percent moderate, eight percent light and 91 percent undamaged.

As of Sunday, eighteen percent of the crop was jointing, compared with one last year and the five-year average of eight percent. Insect and disease infestations remained minimal, with a few reports of armyworms, brown wheat mites and leaf rust in isolated areas.
Seeding of oats advanced to 83 percent complete, ahead of 76 percent last year and the average of 66 percent.

Topsoil moisture condition declined and was rated 21 percent short to very short, 73 adequate and six surplus. The western third of the state continued to report significantly short to very short topsoil moisture, the report said.
